about: Canonical IB Mathematics AA SL syllabus statements (guide for first assessment 2021) and the rules used to tag exam questions. 'content' summarises the guide; 'tagWhen' is the house rule for when a question part earns the tag. 'id' is the permanent statement ID shared with Wasteland Academy's curriculum map; 'courses' lists every course whose syllabus includes the statement. 'subtags' lists the skills inside the statement, with the same ids as Wasteland Academy's skill map; a tagged part's 'sub' names the ones that earn its marks. AA HL adds data/syllabus-aa-hl.json; AI SL and AI HL use data/syllabus-ai.json.
rules: Tag each part by what earns its marks in the markscheme, not by every piece of algebra used along the way.
List the primary statement first. Most parts need 1-2 tags; never more than 3.
Prior learning (expanding, factorising, linear equations, Pythagoras, simple percentages) is never tagged on its own.
A 'show that' calculation is not 1.6 proof. 1.6 is for proving a general statement or identity.
Solving an equation is only tagged 2.10 when no more specific statement covers it (quadratic -> 2.7, trig -> 3.8, exponential/log -> 1.7) or when solving with technology is the point of the part.
If a part says 'hence' and reuses an earlier result, tag only the new content.
